verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA’s 10-day crewed flight test.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Scheduled for almost 10 days, Artemis II won’t land on the moon.'; R3: 'The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R5: 'Duration: 10 days'; R9: 'The 10-day Artemis II mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state ~10-day duration and describe it as a crewed test flight of SLS/Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than September 2025.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'This discovery directly led to the delay of Artemis II’s launch, which was previously scheduled for no earlier than September 2025.'; R7: 'Launch date April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate September 2025 was a previous schedule; actual/planned launch is April 2026, contradicting the claim.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II is set to send humans around the moon.'; R3: 'lifted off ... to begin its journey to deep space.'; R5: 'carrying four astronauts on a journey around the Moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported across sources as a four-astronaut lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human mission to lunar vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first trip astronauts will take outside Earth orbit since 1972'; R2: 'The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed deep space/lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis I and II are test flights'; R7: 'first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as test flight for Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'In 2022, Artemis I tested out ... SLS'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS rocket'; R7: 'second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed SLS flight as a test.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch'
verifications.reasoning: Crew names directly listed in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency'; R3: 'CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Directly confirmed as CSA astronaut in crew lists.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will fly approximately 4,700 miles (7,600 km) beyond the Moon's far side.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'between 5,000 and 9,000 nautical miles beyond the far side of the moon (the actual figure is dependent on the launch date)'
verifications.reasoning: Source gives range of 5,000-9,000 nautical miles (~5,760-10,360 statute miles); 4,700 miles is approximate/lower end but not exact match.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission surpasses previous crewed flight distances.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'This crew will travel farther than any humans ever have before.'; R2: 'set a distance record ... 4,144 miles farther than the Apollo 13'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states it breaks Apollo 13 record.

verifications.claim: The primary goal of Artemis II is to demonstrate that Orion’s life-support systems can keep astronauts safe during a deep-space journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'They’ve learned to operate the spacesuits ... life support system'; 'check out Orion’s systems ... life support'
verifications.reasoning: Sources emphasize testing life support in deep space as key goal.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Victor Glover the first person of color to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mr. Glover ... will be the first Black man to venture into deep space'; R7: 'Victor Glover (an African-American) became the first person of color'
verifications.reasoning: Directly attributed to Glover.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Christina Koch the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Ms. Koch ... will be the first woman to do so.'; R7: 'Christina Koch the first woman'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mr. Hansen ... will be the first person on a moon mission who is not an American.'; R7: 'Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen'
verifications.reasoning: Directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will manually pilot the Orion spacecraft in Earth's orbit to assess its handling.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mr. Glover manually flew the spacecraft'; R3: 'proximity operations demonstration. This demonstration will test the ability to manually maneuver Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Prox ops demo explicitly involves manual piloting in Earth orbit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will perform a 'scenic loop' around the Moon.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'long slingshot around the moon'; 'circling it in a figure eight on a free-return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: 'Scenic loop' not exact term, but describes figure-8 free-return path.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will photograph and study terrain that has not been closely examined in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crew may be able to see parts of the moon humans haven’t experienced before; up to 60 percent of their far side view may be unique ... having human eyes look at the moon up close ... first time ... outside Earth orbit since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Far side observations of terrain not seen by humans in 50+ years.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II team will perform ongoing medical tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'We have three different experiments ... blood draws and wet saliva samples pre- and post-mission ... dry saliva samples ... obstacle course'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple ongoing human research experiments described.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II team will monitor the crew’s health in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Their bodies will also be put to the test ... understand the impacts of space exploration on them ... human research ... psychological well-being and sleep patterns ... assess how space changes the astronauts’ physiology'
verifications.reasoning: Extensive health monitoring in deep space detailed.

verifications.claim: The original designation of Artemis II is Exploration Mission-2 (EM-2).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'Names Artemis II Exploration Mission-2 (EM-2)'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is commonly compared to 21st Century Apollo 8 due to similar orbit mission profile.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The mission, known as Artemis II, is the 21st century equivalent of Apollo 8'; R7: 'objectives were similar to those of Apollo 8'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit comparisons to Apollo 8 as modern equivalent.

verifications.claim: The SLS (Space Launch System) is the 32-story rocket lifting the Artemis II crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '322-foot-tall rocket'
verifications.reasoning: 322 ft ≈ 32 stories (10-11m/story); descriptive but matches height.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft for Artemis II is named Integrity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'spacecraft named Integrity'; R3: 'Orion, named Integrity'; R7: 'Orion CM-003 Integrity'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently named Integrity.

verifications.claim: The European Service Module (ESM-2) powers, propels, and sustains the spacecraft for Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'ESA’s European Service Module, which provides the Orion spacecraft ... with life support, power and propulsion'; R10: 'second European Service Module (ESM-2)'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly matches ESM-2 functions for Artemis II.
